claim_reviews.claim_text: AI and data-center expansion are creating a material increase in electricity demand.
claim_reviews.rationale: DOE provides public quantified demand evidence and J.P. Morgan provides an attributable infrastructure framing. The claim is limited to direction and materiality, not a single global forecast.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Forecast ranges remain wide and depend on AI deployment, efficiency improvements, utilization, and geography.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Review the LBNL report tables and IEA Energy and AI chapters directly to compare methods and regional assumptions.

claim_reviews.claim_text: Grid capacity and interconnection are material constraints on AI data-center deployment.
claim_reviews.rationale: Multiple public official and institutional sources converge on grid capacity, transmission buildout, and interconnection as constraints. This supports the bottleneck at system level, not equal scarcity for every equipment category.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Constraint severity is location-specific and can be mitigated by onsite generation, storage, demand flexibility, and project design.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Add utility interconnection queue data and primary transformer/switchgear lead-time evidence by region.

claim_reviews.claim_text: AI rack-scale systems are increasing power density and forcing changes in power delivery and facility design.
claim_reviews.rationale: NVIDIA product and technical materials directly document rack-scale, liquid-cooled designs and a move beyond traditional low-voltage delivery. Independent standards evidence is still pending.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Vendor roadmaps do not prove the timing or market-wide prevalence of a given rack power level.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Acquire OCP specifications and independent operator deployment data for rack power distributions.

claim_reviews.claim_text: 800 VDC is an emerging technical route for reducing conversion stages and supporting denser future AI racks.
claim_reviews.rationale: NVIDIA publicly documents the architecture and intended benefits. The claim is reviewed only as a declared technical route, not as a proven deployment standard or revenue forecast.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Adoption timing, interoperability, safety standards, transition architectures, and supplier allocation remain unsettled.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Review exact OCP specifications, operator reference designs, and disclosed deployments.

claim_reviews.claim_text: High-density rack-scale AI systems can require liquid cooling to manage density and floor-space constraints.
claim_reviews.rationale: The reviewed NVIDIA product page directly identifies a liquid-cooled rack-scale design and links liquid cooling to compute density. It does not establish universal adoption or supplier economics.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Cooling architecture varies by accelerator generation, rack design, climate, facility retrofit constraints, and operator preference.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Add independent operator specifications, cooling BOM data, certification requirements, and full-text domestic broker evidence.

claim_reviews.claim_text: Higher AI rack power necessarily means copper interconnect captures more value across all architectures.
claim_reviews.rationale: NVIDIA's 800 VDC materials explicitly target lower current, copper use, and cable bulk. Aggregate data-center buildout may still raise copper demand, but the blanket per-architecture value-capture claim is not valid.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Total copper demand depends on data-center capacity growth, voltage architecture, cable length, busway design, and material substitution.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Build a scenario model separating total installed capacity from copper intensity per delivered megawatt.

claim_reviews.claim_text: All transformers, switchgear, UPS, PDU, and power-conversion suppliers benefit uniformly from the 800 VDC transition.
claim_reviews.rationale: The proposed 800 VDC route reduces conversion stages and can remove or relocate some conventional equipment layers. Value transfer must be assessed by architecture and component function, not by a blanket beneficiary list.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Transition-period hybrid designs may increase spending in some categories even if mature architectures simplify the power train.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Compare current AC, hybrid 800 VDC, and native 800 VDC BOMs and identify which functions expand, shrink, or move.

claim_reviews.claim_text: Specific AI power nodes have material China localization gaps that create investable domestic substitution opportunities.
claim_reviews.rationale: No accepted public source in this pack establishes product-level import dependence, domestic qualification status, revenue materiality, or customer adoption for Chinese listed companies.
claim_reviews.uncertainty: Localization conditions differ by voltage class, component specification, customer certification, and project geography.
claim_reviews.next_evidence_needed: Acquire exact broker reports, company filings, customer qualification disclosures, customs data, and product-level market-share evidence.
